title: 2021 AMC 12B Problem 11
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) has \(AB=13,\) \(BC=14,\) and \(AC=15.\) Let \(P\) be the point on \(\overline{AC}\) such that \(PC=10.\) There are exactly two points \(D\) and \(E\) on line \(BP\) such that quadrilaterals \(ABCD\) and \(ABCE\) are trapezoids. What is the distance \(DE?\)

solutions.text:
Place \(A=(0,0)\) and \(C=(15,0).\) Then \(B=\left(\tfrac{33}{5},\tfrac{56}{5}\right),\) and since \(PC=10,\) \(P=(5,0).\) Line \(BP\) has slope \(7,\) so it is \(y=7(x-5).\)

For \(ABCD\) to be a trapezoid with \(D\) on line \(BP,\) take \(CD\parallel AB.\) The line through \(C\) parallel to \(AB\) meets line \(BP\) at \((\tfrac95,-\tfrac{112}{5}).\)

For \(ABCE\) with \(E\) on line \(BP,\) take \(AE\parallel BC.\) The line through \(A\) parallel to \(BC\) meets line \(BP\) at \((\tfrac{21}{5},-\tfrac{28}{5}).\)

Their coordinate differences are \(\tfrac{12}{5}\) and \(\tfrac{84}{5},\) so \(DE=\tfrac15\sqrt{12^2+84^2}=12\sqrt2.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: One trapezoid needs \(CD\parallel AB,\) the other needs \(AE\parallel BC;\) find where each parallel line meets line \(BP\)
